experiments.guard: NEW: live_bound() must ask systemd for SLICE units — the discovery query is what makes the whole feature find an operator's memcap.slice at all. Asking for the wrong unit type makes live_bound() return None on every real box (the .slice filter drops every returned name), i.e. `doctor` says OFF forever, which is precisely the bug CMX-280 exists to end

NEW: _slice_memory() must ask systemd for MemoryMax — the property docs/RESOURCE_ISOLATION.md's own 'Verify, don't assume' section checks by hand, and the one the parser then reads back with values.get('MemoryMax'). Asking for MemoryHigh (a real, different systemd property — the soft limit) means the MemoryMax key is never present in real output, so _finite(None) -> None -> live_bound() returns None and the feature is dead on every real box

NEW: live_bound()'s tie-break, as its own docstring states it — 'the slice with the LEAST headroom (max_bytes - current_bytes, or max_bytes alone when occupancy is unreadable)'. Collapsing the unreadable-occupancy case to 0 makes any slice whose MemoryCurrent could not be read always win, hiding the real 12G/10G bound an operator needs to see behind a slice chela knows nothing about
experiments.before: headroom = max_bytes if current_bytes is None else max_bytes - current_bytes
experiments.after: headroom = 0 if current_bytes is None else max_bytes - current_bytes

experiments.guard: live_bound()'s discovery query must ask systemd for ACTIVE slices — round 4's own fix (DEFEAT_SHAPES #24: 'assert the full trailing argv the fake dispatches on, not just the prefix it routes on') was applied to only ONE of the two call sites. _fake_show now asserts the full tail (cmd[4:] == _SHOW_PROPS), but _fake_list_and_show asserts only membership of a single flag (`'--type=slice' in cmd`), leaving --state=active, --no-legend, --plain and --no-pager as invisible to the suite as --type=slice was last round. Flipping --state=active to --state=inactive makes _list_user_slices() enumerate units that are NOT running — measured on this box, `systemctl --user list-units --type=slice --state=inactive` returns ZERO units while the active query returns memcap.slice — so live_bound() returns None on every real box and `doctor` says OFF forever, which is precisely the bug CMX-280 exists to end.
